title: Determine supported GP8 trill-speed encoding
scope: Resolve the current forced sixteenth-note trill duration using actual target syntax and independent consumption.
acceptance: Compare authored 16th, 32nd and 64th trill speeds at the same non-default fret.
Identify a supported GPIF speed payload, or show that the target consumer has a fixed value.
Preserve supported speeds or retain the exact normalization policy, with no false full-support rating.

reproduction.instructions: Compare authored 16th, 32nd and 64th trill speeds at the same non-default fret.

evidence.detail: Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.
Existing scoped evidence; not proof of all AlphaTab variants.
target-limit: GPIF carries target fret but pinned parsing fixes duration to sixteenth. Do not repurpose rhythm or tremolo as speed.

Use the same non-default target fret with authored 16th, 32nd and 64th speeds. Assert exact Trill wire value, the pinned consumer sixteenth result and the precise normalization report. Verify that sixteenth input incurs no speed loss while non-sixteenth input is rejected under strict preservation unless the exact loss is allowed. Resolve as the documented speed limit after verification. Do not encode speed using rhythm, tremolo or ornament properties; those change other authored semantics.
